title: Having a hard time picking between GPT and Claude rn. Any more experienced dev got tips on if I should go for either?
author: Alarming_Scientist
selftext:
I was initially gonna go for Claude max but then i faced the problem of verification shitting the bed and completely preventing me from using claude further. I'm thinking of just going for GPT instead after that experience. But I've heard Claude's simply better for coding games. 

  
Is Claude worth it to wait for support to fix my issue or should i just go for GPT?

  
(Legit no clue what was happening, refused to read my passport and then completely refused to even bring up the verification screen. annoying as hell ngl.)

comments.author: jamurai
comments.body: Claude easily if you can only pick one and want a more polished looking and feeling game. My understanding is Claude can’t really image gen if you want to set up game assets with, which codex is quite good at. But you can probably use some online models for image gen or just image gen directly with something like tripo (assuming 3d).

comments.author: IntelligentDot2924
comments.body: I am throwing my hat in the ring and saying neither get Ollama Cloud and try their offerings with OpenCode.

comments.author: IAmhowlshot
comments.body:
I have both, Claude is light-years ahead for game dev at the moment. 
Openai has neutered their models

comments.author: count023
comments.body: claude for more creative design work and ui front end stuff, codex if you're doing grunty logic and back end work or reverse engineering.

comments.author: MichaelEmouse
comments.body: Look up comparisons on YouTube. Claude high/extra seems to be the sweet spot.

replies.author: wewerecreaturres
replies.body: This is the way. Opus 5.5 xhigh for thinking/planning, drop down to medium for implement. Haven’t checked sonnet 5.5 but I’d bet it could be the implementer now

replies.author: MichaelEmouse
replies.body: I find that Max will have the occasional insight that high and extra don't the I implement in extra since implementation of a prototype is a lot larger than the preceding discussion. The videos I saw on YouTube usually showed high and extra as the best aside from Ultra Code.

replies.author: wewerecreaturres
replies.body: Ultra code is just xhigh with subagents

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body: Honestly I can’t tell too much of a difference in quality between them but most people say Claude so I’m guessing there is a reason.

comments.author: Minimum_Lock_1906
comments.body: Se você tiver condições, Opus 5.5 para arquitetura e Sol 6.1 para Codificação (No mínimo). O Astra é fenomenal porém sendo sincero não acredito que valha o custo quando o Sol 6.1 está tendo um excelente desempenho.

comments.author: Asleepius_Games
comments.body: I go cursor and then just switch models when i need. Use claude for about 5% of heavy task where I need reliability, then the built-in grok for everything else and it does wonders. I keep the chat fired up all day and never run past my limit and use any extra tokens beyond the $60 sub.

comments.author: Varrianda
comments.body: I still use both, but right now the Claude $200 plan is a substantially better deal than codex’s $200 plan. I just prefer Astra for creative work.

comments.author: sw3d
comments.body: Claude and it's not even close, Argon 4 can't compete either

comments.author: wewerecreaturres
comments.body: They all have their strengths. For pure code, nothing touches Claude. I find gpt better at creative writing. Haven’t compared across them for asset stuff.

comments.author: OmniNL
comments.body:
If you like taking breaks and enjoying nature, GPT's limits and token allowances give you plenty of opportunities to do that. If you want to get 5x as much work done and only take a short coffee break while waiting for your tokens to reset, choose Claude.

I use both.

(Or maybe I'm using them wrong. I orchestrate with Opus 5.5, implement with Sonnet 5.5, or use GPT 6.1 SOL for both.)
